answer: Put a reserve price on every job from median honest cost, then assign it by second-price auction. Bidders post prices in cipher envelopes that open together at the horizon of the window, so nobody can whisper a lower price after seeing a rival's. The lowest bid above the reserve wins but is paid the second-lowest price, and a winner that walks away forfeits a bond. A farm of 1,000 clones underbidding to grab volume must deliver each job at a loss or bleed bonds, $500 an epoch, while one honest agent bids its true cost. Like a fish market where the catch goes to the lowest honest stall.
